movement_source: row 'Net interest margin (%)', column 30 Jun 25 full-year column -> column 30 Jun 26 full-year column
headline: CBA's Group net interest margin fell 3 bps to 2.05% in FY26 from 2.08% in FY25 (KPI table, cash basis; the FY25 book printed the same 2.08%). Net interest income rose $1,563m or 7% to $25,586m on an 8% rise in average interest earning assets to $1,246bn. The results book's walk: asset pricing −5 bps (home lending −4, business & institutional −1, competition), liquids −3, Treasury & Markets −2, offset by Capital, Replicating and Other +5 (replicating portfolio +4, capital hedges +1) and portfolio mix +2; funding costs and basis risk flat. The presentation's framing combines institutional repos with liquids (Liquids & repos −4; Treasury & Markets −1). Excluding growth in liquid assets, which the bank says have broadly neutral impacts on net interest income, NIM was stable — the decline is a denominator drag plus lending-pricing pressure, offset by hedge earnings and favourable mix.

drivers.narrative: Home lending pricing down 4 bps and business and institutional lending pricing down 1 bp, 'primarily reflecting the impact of competition'. Slide sub-split: home loan competition (3), impact of cash rate lag (1), business & insto. lending (1).

Liquid asset average balances rose $15bn or 9% to $187bn. The bank says liquid assets 'have broadly neutral impacts on net interest income', so this bar is a denominator drag on the ratio, not lost income; excluding it, NIM was stable.

'due to lower risk management income in Treasury and growth in reverse sale and repurchase agreement balances.' The slide shows (1) here because it carries institutional repos in its combined Liquids & repos bar instead.

'driven by higher earnings on the replicating portfolio due to changes in portfolio rate and volume (up 4 basis points) and higher earnings on capital hedges (up 1 basis point).' Slide: replicating portfolio 4, higher earnings on capital 1.

'favourable asset mix from strong growth in business lending and favourable funding mix from strong growth in deposits.' Business and corporate average balances rose $27bn or 10% to $299bn; slide: 'deposits growing faster than lending'.
Published zero bar: 'Funding costs: Flat.' The bank discloses no further reason for the full-year comparison; funding costs contributed nothing to the FY26 vs FY25 margin movement.
Published zero bar: 'Basis risk: Flat.' The bank discloses no reason for the full-year comparison; basis risk contributed nothing to the FY26 vs FY25 margin movement.

notable_items: None — the NIM movement contains no notable items; the bank's qualification is that growth in liquid assets and institutional reverse sale and repurchase agreements has broadly neutral impacts on net interest income.
limitations: The results book and the presentation publish different framings of the same walk: the book shows Liquids −3 and Treasury & Markets −2; the slide shows combined Liquids & repos −4 (liquid assets −3, institutional repos −1) and Treasury & Markets −1. Both sum to −3; the book framing is adopted per results-book primacy.

The −3 bps liquids bar is a denominator effect: the bank states liquid assets and institutional reverse sale and repurchase agreements 'have broadly neutral impacts on net interest income' and that NIM excluding their growth was stable. The underlying margin decline is therefore smaller than the headline −3 bps.

The slide's asset-pricing sub-split (home loan competition −3, cash rate lag −1, business & insto. lending −1) is slide-level annotation and does not reconcile line-for-line with the book's home lending −4 / business and institutional −1 split.

The Group NIM row carries no cash or statutory label; it is reported here on the bank's primary (cash) basis per the KPI table footnote 'Presented on a cash basis unless stated otherwise', on a continuing-operations basis in the NII table.
The presentation's zero Funding costs bar is printed as a dash ('-') in the chart text layer; its zero value is read from the chart image (ev-12), not from a printed numeral.

evidence_records.quote: Net interest income was $25,586 million, an increase of $1,563 million or 7% on the prior year. The result was driven by a $92 billion or 8% increase in average interest earning assets to $1,246 billion, partly offset by a 3 basis point decrease in net interest margin to 2.05%.

The Bank’s net interest margin decreased by 3 basis points on the prior year to 2.05%. Excluding growth in liquid assets, which have broadly neutral impacts on net interest income, net interest margin was stable.

Asset pricing: Decreased margin by 5 basis points driven by home lending pricing (down 4 basis points) and business and institutional lending pricing (down 1 basis point), primarily reflecting the impact of competition.
